title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: custom engine agents for GCC High users
summary: Hold: the low cost rating treats paid hosting and model consumption as indirect costs, and the licensing discussion overlooks published platform access rules. The roadmap facts and both control references check out, but several limitations need their documented scope retained.

claims.claim: The roadmap states that GCC High users will be able to use custom engine agents.
claims.quote: Users in GCC-H will be able to use custom engine agents.

claims.quote: These agents can be created using Copilot Studio, the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK, Teams SDK or Microsoft Foundry, depending on your preferred development approach and hosting environment.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Custom engine agents typically use hosting outside Microsoft 365, with builder-controlled processing and additional hosting costs.
claims.quote: Require additional hosting outside of Microsoft 365, typically with cloud services such as Azure, at an additional cost.
claims.fix: Qualify the hosting statements, including licensing.notes and the risk rationale: 'Pro-code custom engine agents use builder-provided orchestration and hosting; Copilot Studio provides a managed alternative.' The same comparison table says 'Hosted in Microsoft 365 with Copilot Studio or externally with custom solutions such as Azure AI', and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/overview-custom-engine-agent describes Copilot Studio as fully managed.

claims.claim: Custom engine agent prompts and responses in Copilot Chat and Teams are stored under Microsoft 365 product terms.
claims.quote: Custom engine agent prompts and responses in Copilot Chat and Teams are stored in compliance with Microsoft 365 product terms and conditions and are managed as per the customer's instructions.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model and required user licences are wholly unpublished for this GCC High release.
claims.quote:
| Custom engine agents | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
Usage-based billing isn't supported in Microsoft 365 Government Community Cloud High (GCCH) and Government Community Cloud (GCC) environments.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'mixed'. Replace the blanket licensing-unknown statements with 'Learn lists custom engine agents for Copilot Chat users without usage-based billing and for licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot users. Builder-operated hosting and models have separate costs. Usage-based billing is not supported in GCC or GCCH; a separate licence or meter specific to this GCC High release is not named.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/prerequisites and the existing hosting/cost sources. Narrow the licensing open question to any release-specific requirements, rather than whether any access model has been published.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Cost is low because hosting, models and orchestration are indirect costs only.
claims.quote: Briefing: 'Low. The only cost the sources show is indirect: hosting, models and orchestration that the agent's builder provides.' Learn: 'Instead, the cost depends on the Azure services consumed in the app.'
claims.fix: Set cost to 'variable'. Replace the cost rationale with 'Variable. Builder-operated agents can incur Azure hosting and model consumption charges; a separate meter specific to this GCC High release is not named.' Replace 'Hosting and admin time are the indirect costs' with 'Hosting and model usage are direct service costs; admin time is an indirect cost.' Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/faq to sources. The schema reserves low for indirect costs only and defines variable for metered Azure consumption.
